text:
alex: Heads up — noticed console quicksearch prefetch returning results that include rows from other orgs when folks rapidly switch workspaces. Repro steps below. :eyes:

jess: ugh, can you paste an example log line?

alex: sure, from pref-worker logs:```[prefetch-worker] ts=2026-03-21T15:02:11Z session=abcd1234 org=org-42 prefetch_key=search::q=errors user=ryan -> resp.items:[org-42,org-99]```

maria: hmm prefetch_key looks suspicious — is that only keyed by session?

alex: yep, we only used session cookie + query string. X-Org-ID header wasn't included in the key. Race case: same session across tabs + worker pool reuse.

ryan: that would cause cached payload to be served in wrong org context. Also impacts quota attribution and telemetry labels.

jess: how frequent? any customer-facing incidents?

alex: small numbers but real: ~0.002% of quicksearch requests in last hour had mixed org ids, saw trace id `trace-0xdeadbeef`. No PII exposed in examples I checked.

maria: still problematic for billing/quotas and rollouts. Hypothesis: prefetcher LRU keyed by session only + pooled worker responding after org switch.

ryan: quick mitigation suggestions:
- include `X-Org-ID` (and workspace) in cache key
- add server-side validation before returning cached response: ensure all item.org == request.org
- when mismatch detected, evict and re-fetch
- short-term: disable reuse for 5s after an org switch event for a session

jess: +1. Add a telemetry counter when mismatch occurs so we can monitor. `prefetch.cache.org_mismatch`

alex: proposed minimal code change (prefetcher):
```python
cache_key = f\"prefetch:{session_id}:{org_id}:{query_hash}\"
cached = cache.get(cache_key)
if cached and all(item[\"org\"] == org_id for item in cached[\"items\"]):
    return cached
else:
    resp = backend.fetch(q)
    cache.set(cache_key, resp)
    return resp
```

maria: also add an assert in the debug path that drops the cached result and increments `prefetch.cache.org_mismatch` metric so we can catch any edge cases.

ryan: I'll open a hotfix PR and tag for emergency rollout. Canary to 5% then monitor, move to 50% if stable.

alex: QA: I'll write a unit test simulating concurrent org swap across two requests with same session id; expect the cache to separate keys or validation to fallback to real fetch.

jess: dashboard work: create a panel showing `prefetch.cache.org_mismatch` and `prefetch.cache.hits_by_org` and alert if mismatch > 10 in 1h.

maria: confirmed telemetry will be updated to include `prefetch.source_org` and `prefetch.returned_orgs` array for debugging. We'll redact anything sensitive.

ryan: PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/1234 (mock). Assigning @maria for telemetry, @alex for QA, @jess for rollout decision.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary 5% at 6876544500 by @ryan. :rocket:

jess: One more thought — this also affects quota routing. If we return results containing other org ids, downstream quota attribution might think resources used belong to wrong org. Need coordination with billing team before wide rollout.

alex: good call, I'll ping @billing. But urgent fix should go ahead with canary; telemetry + billing sync before 50%.

maria: I'll add a temporary gate in the routing layer to double-check response orgs for the next 48h. If mismatch seen, route request to dedicated path and increment incident counter.

ryan: ETA for hotfix PR review + staging tests: 60m. Can we get sign-off for canary after 1h of green staging?

jess: yes. If staging stable, roll the canary and notify eng-oncall.

alex: created a short playbook entry in #incidents and will dump repro script + logs there.

maria: dashboard created: https://graf.redwood/d/abcd/prefetch-metrics (mock). Alert rule set.

ryan: merging to staging after CI.

alex: thanks team — small bug, low volume, but glad we caught it before a customer noticed. :ok_hand:
